title: Vascular and non-vascular intervention

steps.tx: A **Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt** (TIPS) decompresses portal hypertension by creating an artificial low-resistance conduit between the right hepatic vein and the right portal vein. Deployed with an expanded polytetrafluoroethylene stent graft, TIPS reduces the **portosystemic gradient** to below 12 mm Hg to manage refractory ascites and recurrent variceal hemorrhage.
steps.say: A Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt decompresses portal hypertension by creating an artificial low-resistance conduit between the right hepatic vein and the right portal vein. Deployed with an expanded polytetrafluoroethylene stent graft, TIPS reduces the portosystemic gradient to below 12 millimetres of mercury to manage refractory ascites and recurrent variceal hemorrhage.

vis.alt: Fluoroscopic image demonstrating TIPS stent deployment between right hepatic vein and portal vein
vis.caption: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt connecting portal and hepatic veins

steps.tx: Endovascular **embolisation agents** are classified into temporary mechanical agents like gelatin sponge or **Gelfoam** (resorbed in 2 to 6 weeks) and permanent agents. Permanent agents include metallic microcoils, polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) particles, n-butyl cyanoacrylate tissue adhesive, and Onyx ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer.
steps.say: Endovascular embolisation agents are classified into temporary mechanical agents like gelatin sponge or Gelfoam, which is resorbed in 2 to 6 weeks, and permanent agents. Permanent agents can contain metallic microcoils, polyvinyl alcohol particles, n-butyl cyanoacrylate tissue adhesive, and Onyx ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer.

rows: Resorbed over 2 to 6 weeks; temporary haemostasis
Permanent microvascular occlusion at arteriolar level
Permanent mechanical obstruction with induced thrombosis
Permanent cast polymerizing upon contact with blood

steps.tx: An iatrogenic femoral **pseudoaneurysm** exhibits a characteristic **yin-yang sign** on colour Doppler ultrasound due to swirling bidirectional turbulent flow within the extravascular communicating sac. When neck anatomy is favourable, ultrasound-guided percutaneous thrombin injection achieves thrombosis exceeding 95% of cases without requiring open surgical repair.

left.title: Pseudoaneurysm Features
points: Swirling yin-yang sign on colour Doppler

right.title: Uncomplicated Haematoma
points: Absence of internal colour Doppler flow
No direct communication with femoral artery

steps.tx: **Transarterial chemoembolisation** (TACE) combines targeted intra-arterial infusion of chemotherapy (doxorubicin or cisplatin emulsified in **Lipiodol**) with particulate embolisation. Chemoembolization induces selective ischaemic necrosis of hypervascular hepatocellular carcinomas while sparing normal liver parenchyma that receives 75% of its perfusion from the portal vein.
steps.say: Transarterial chemoembolisation combines targeted intra-arterial infusion of chemotherapy, such as doxorubicin or cisplatin emulsified in Lipiodol, with particulate embolisation. Chemoembolization induces selective ischaemic necrosis of hypervascular hepatocellular carcinomas while sparing normal liver parenchyma that receives 75% of its perfusion from the portal vein.

vis.alt: Angiographic and CT image demonstrating transcatheter arterial chemoembolization of hepatocellular carcinoma
vis.caption: Selective hepatic artery catheterization and lipiodol retention during TACE

steps.tx: Percutaneous **radiofrequency ablation** and microwave ablation induce thermal coagulative necrosis of hepatic malignancies through targeted heating. Achieving complete oncological eradication requires a minimum 5 to 10 mm circumferential **ablative margin** of normal liver parenchyma beyond gross tumor boundaries to prevent local microscopic recurrence.
steps.say: Percutaneous radiofrequency ablation and microwave ablation help to induce thermal coagulative necrosis of hepatic malignancies through targeted heating. Achieving complete oncological eradication requires a minimum 5 to 10 millimetre circumferential ablative margin of normal liver parenchyma beyond gross tumor boundaries to prevent local microscopic recurrence.

left.title: Ablative Margin Criteria
points: Minimum 5 to 10 mm normal margin required

right.title: Heat Sink Pitfall
points: Dissipation of thermal energy by blood flow
Microwave ablation less prone than RFA

steps.tx: **May-Thurner syndrome** involves extrinsic compression of the left common **iliac vein** by the overlying right common iliac artery against the fifth lumbar vertebra (L5). Chronic arterial pulsation triggers endothelial trauma, venous web formation, and acute left iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis, treated successfully with endovascular self-expanding nitinol stenting.

rows: Transmits systolic arterial pulsation against vein
Luminal spur and fibrous web formation
Rigid osseous backstop preventing posterior displacement
Overcomes mechanical recoil and prevents recurrent DVT

steps.tx: Percutaneous transhepatic **biliary drainage** (PTBD) is performed under fluoroscopic or ultrasound guidance by puncturing a peripheral bile duct (segment 3 on the left or segment 6 on the right) to decompress severe **obstructive jaundice**. External-internal drainage restores physiological bile flow across malignant biliary strictures.
steps.say: Percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage is performed under fluoroscopic or ultrasound guidance by puncturing a peripheral bile duct, ideally segment 3 on the left or segment 6 on the right, to decompress severe obstructive jaundice. External-internal drainage helps to restore physiological bile flow across malignant biliary strictures.

vis.alt: Fluoroscopic image demonstrating biliary drainage catheter traversing stricture
vis.caption: Percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage catheter decompressing obstructed biliary tree

steps.tx: Retrievable **Inferior vena cava filter** placement is indicated for acute venous thromboembolism with absolute contraindications to anticoagulation. The apex of the filter is positioned immediately below the lowest **renal vein** orifice to prevent filter tilting and mitigate bilateral renal venous thrombosis.

rows: Positioned immediately below lowest renal vein
Avoids renal vein thrombosis and turbulent flow
Transverse diameter ≤ 28 mm for standard filters
Prevents filter migration into pulmonary circulation
Maintains clot capture efficiency and retrievability
Avoids chronic caval penetration and IVC occlusion
